# SVG to Slides — editable SVGs in Google Slides

SVG to Slides is a free Chrome extension that inserts SVG files into Google Slides as native, editable shapes.

Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

- Install: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter (no install): https://svgslid.es/convert
- Google Slides add-on: https://svgslid.es/addon

## The problem
Google Slides doesn't support SVG files. Your options are to flatten them into PNGs or take the long way through EMF conversion, Google Drawings, and copy-paste.

## What it does
- **Edit individual elements.** Every SVG path becomes its own Slides shape. Recolour any element with the standard fill picker.
- **Resize without losing quality.** From a small footer icon to a full-slide graphic, every edge stays sharp.
- **Use SVGs in your themes.** Add converted graphics to theme layouts and reuse them across slides.

## How it works
1. Install the extension from the Chrome Web Store. No account required.
2. Open Google Slides, in any existing or new presentation.
3. Drag in your SVG. Its paths become editable shapes.

## Limits
- Gradients come through in the online converter; in the extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.
- Arc commands (A/a) are converted into smooth curves.
- Up to 25 files per drop in the extension; use the online converter for larger batches.

## Privacy
The Chrome extension converts on your device with an embedded WebAssembly engine; your file usually never leaves the browser. Details: https://svgslid.es/privacy


---

# SVG to Google Slides converter (online)

Upload SVG files at https://svgslid.es/convert and get a Slides-ready file in Google Drive with real, editable vector shapes.

1. Upload one or more .svg files. Each SVG becomes one slide.
2. Every `<path>` becomes its own native, individually selectable shape in Google Slides, not a flattened image.
3. The file is uploaded to Google Drive and a link is returned, optionally shared to a Google account you provide.

- Links are deleted after 7 days. To keep a file, open it in Drive and choose File → Make a copy.
- Solid fills, strokes and gradients come through. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves.

Working in a deck already? The free Chrome extension drops SVGs straight onto a slide: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

# SVG vs PNG in Google Slides™

When Google Slides flattens an SVG it becomes a single image that blurs when resized and can't be recoloured or edited. SVG to Slides converts every path into Slides' own native shape format instead, so the result behaves like a shape you drew yourself.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Flattened vs. converted

| Pasted as PNG (default) | Inserted with SVG to Slides |
|---|---|
| Blurs or pixelates when resized | Resizes at any size, always crisp |
| One flattened image, single object | Every path is its own selectable shape |
| Can't recolour without re-exporting | Recolour any shape directly in Slides |
| Can't animate individual elements | Animate each shape independently |
| Can't edit points or paths | Right-click → Edit points, like any native shape |

## Pick your route
- **Chrome extension** — Drag an SVG file straight onto an open Slides tab and drop it in place. No dialog, no upload step. (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi)
- **Web Uploader** — Upload one or more SVGs and get back a Google Drive link to a ready-made Slides file, one slide per SVG. (https://svgslid.es/convert)
- **Google Slides add-on** — Insert SVGs into a presentation you're already editing, from a dialog inside Slides itself. (https://svgslid.es/addon)

## How it stays a vector
- Every <path> in your SVG is converted directly into Google Slides' own native shape format. It isn't re-rendered as an image and it isn't a third-party embed.
- The result behaves exactly like a shape you drew in Slides yourself: resizable, recolourable, editable.

## Questions

### Does Google Slides support SVG natively?
Not as an editable format. Slides rasterizes an inserted SVG into a flattened image, so you lose the ability to edit individual paths or recolour parts of it. SVG to Slides converts it into Slides' native shape format instead, so it stays fully editable.

### What happens to gradients and complex curves?
Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.

### Is my file uploaded anywhere?
Depends on the surface. The Chrome extension converts entirely on your device using an embedded WebAssembly engine, so your file usually never leaves the browser. The online converter and add-on send the file to our backend for conversion. See the privacy policy for specifics.

### Is it free?
Yes. Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

# Insert an SVG into Google Slides™

Google Slides doesn't accept SVG files as editable graphics. To insert one, install the free SVG to Slides Chrome extension, open your presentation, and drag the .svg file onto a slide. Each path becomes its own native Slides shape.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## How to do it
1. **Install the extension.** Add SVG to Slides from the Chrome Web Store. No account required.
2. **Open Google Slides.** Work in any existing or new presentation.
3. **Drag in your SVG.** Drop the file onto a slide. Its paths become editable shapes. Up to 25 files per drop.

## Other ways in
- Web converter. Upload SVGs at svgslid.es/convert and get a Google Drive link to a Slides-ready file, one slide per SVG. No install.
- Google Slides add-on. Insert SVGs from a dialog inside Slides, without leaving the tab. Get the add-on.
- The long way. Without a converter, your options are flattening the SVG to a PNG, or EMF conversion, Google Drawings, and copy-paste.

## Questions

### Can I upload an SVG to Google Slides directly?
Not as an editable graphic. Without a converter, your options are to flatten it into a PNG or take the long way through EMF conversion, Google Drawings, and copy-paste. SVG to Slides converts the file into native Slides shapes instead.

### How many SVGs can I insert at once?
Up to 25 per drop with the Chrome extension. For larger batches, use the bulk converter at svgslid.es/convert.

### Does it cost anything?
Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

### Is my file uploaded anywhere?
The Chrome extension converts on your device using an embedded WebAssembly engine, so your file usually never leaves the browser. The web converter and add-on send the file to our backend for conversion.

# Does Google Slides™ support SVG?

No. Google Slides doesn't keep SVG files as editable vectors. Your options are to flatten the SVG into a PNG, or convert it through EMF and Google Drawings. SVG to Slides converts the file into Slides' native shape format, so it stays editable.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Flattened vs. converted

| Pasted as PNG (default) | Inserted with SVG to Slides |
|---|---|
| Blurs or pixelates when resized | Resizes at any size, always crisp |
| One flattened image, single object | Every path is its own selectable shape |
| Can't recolour without re-exporting | Recolour any shape directly in Slides |
| Can't animate individual elements | Animate each shape independently |
| Can't edit points or paths | Right-click → Edit points, like any native shape |

## Questions

### Can you import an SVG into Google Slides?
Not as editable vector shapes. Install the SVG to Slides Chrome extension and drag the file onto a slide, or upload it at svgslid.es/convert. Both turn every path into a native Slides shape.

### Why does my SVG look blurry in Google Slides?
It's been flattened into a raster image, so it pixelates when you resize it. Converted with SVG to Slides, it stays a vector and every edge stays sharp.

### What happens to gradients and complex curves?
Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.

### Do the converted shapes work in Google Drawings?
Yes. The native shapes also work in Google Drawings.

SVG to Slides converts SVG files into native, editable Google Slides shapes. Use the Chrome extension to drop files straight onto a slide, or the web converter to turn a batch of SVGs into a Slides-ready file in Google Drive. Every surface is free.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Pick your route
- **Chrome extension** — Drag an SVG straight onto an open Slides tab and drop it in place. No dialog, no upload step. Converts in your browser. (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi)
- **Web Uploader** — Upload one or more SVGs and get back a Google Drive link to a Slides-ready file, one slide per SVG. Best for bulk conversion or building an icon library. (https://svgslid.es/convert)
- **Google Slides add-on** — Insert SVGs into a presentation you're already editing, from a dialog inside Slides itself. (https://svgslid.es/addon)

## Questions

### Is there an online SVG to Google Slides converter?
Yes. Upload SVGs at svgslid.es/convert. No install needed. You get a Google Drive link to a file with one slide per SVG.

### Do I need an account?
No account is required for the extension. The web converter takes an optional Google account email if you want the file shared directly to you.

### How long does the web converter keep my file?
The link stays active for 7 days. To keep a file, open it in Drive and choose File → Make a copy. The copy is fully yours, with no expiry.

### Is it really free?
Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

# Edit and recolor SVGs in Google Slides™

Once converted with SVG to Slides, every path in your SVG is a separate native Slides shape. Select one element and change its fill with the standard picker, edit its points, or animate it on its own.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## What you can do
- **Select individual elements.** Every path is its own selectable shape, not one flattened image.
- **Recolour with the fill picker.** Change any shape's colour directly in Slides. No re-exporting.
- **Edit points.** Right-click → Edit points, like any shape you drew yourself.
- **Animate each shape.** Build transitions element by element instead of animating one image.

## Questions

### Can I change the color of an SVG in Google Slides?
Yes, once it's converted. SVG to Slides turns each path into a native shape, so you can recolour any element with the standard fill picker.

### Can I edit the points of an SVG shape?
Yes. Right-click a converted shape and choose Edit points, like any native shape.

### What about gradients?
Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.

# SVG logos and icons in Google Slides™ themes

Convert your logo or icon set with SVG to Slides, add it to your theme layouts, and reuse it on every slide. The shapes resize without losing quality and also work in Google Drawings.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## What you can do
- **Use SVGs in your themes.** Put converted logos and icons in theme layouts so they appear on every slide that uses them.
- **Resize without losing quality.** From a small footer icon to a full-slide graphic, every edge stays sharp.
- **Build an icon library.** Upload a batch at svgslid.es/convert and get one slide per icon, ready to copy from.
- **Works in Google Drawings.** The native shapes also work in Google Drawings.

## Questions

### Can I put an SVG logo in a Google Slides theme?
Yes. Convert it with SVG to Slides, then add it to your theme layouts. It stays a native, resizable shape.

### How do I convert a whole icon set?
Upload the files at svgslid.es/convert. You get a Google Drive link to a file with one slide per SVG.

### Will my logo stay sharp when I scale it?
Yes. Converted shapes are vectors, so they resize at any size and stay crisp.

# Google Slides finally does letter spacing

*Nov 7, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Tracking has landed in Google Slides. Here's what it is, how to use it well, and why Docs looks next.

## TL;DR
- Slides now has **letter spacing**, which type designers call **tracking**.
- Toolbar: the **|A|** button next to line spacing. Menu: **Format › Text › Letter spacing**.
- Presets: **6, 3, 0, −1.5**, plus **Custom spacing** (any value, decimals and negatives allowed; no unit shown).
- The Docs help center documents it; the Docs editor doesn't show it yet (as of Nov 7, 2026).

## Tracking vs. kerning vs. leading
- Tracking: same space added/removed after every letter in a selection (the new control).
- Kerning: space between one specific pair (e.g. AV); set by the font, not exposed in Slides.
- Leading: space between lines; the line spacing button.

## Tips
1. Open up all-caps text and small labels (+3 to +6).
2. Tighten large display headlines slightly (−1.5).
3. Leave body text at 0.
4. Bigger type → tighter; smaller type → looser.
5. Positive values widen lines: recheck line breaks and text box overflow.
6. One value per role (eyebrow, headline, body) for consistency.
7. Check in Present mode.

## Steps
1. Select text or a whole text box.
2. Click Letter spacing (|A|) in the toolbar, or Format › Text › Letter spacing.
3. Pick 6, 3, 0 or −1.5. Or choose Custom spacing, enter a value, Apply.
4. Reset by choosing 0.

## The slip-up that points to Docs
- Docs help article "Change how paragraphs & fonts look" (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349) now has an "Adjust letter spacing" section (text, text boxes, tables; toolbar button and Format › Text › Letter spacing).
- Wayback Machine: absent on Oct 5, 2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/20261005194616/https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349?rd=1&visit_id=639268263719815361-3052973569); present Oct 12, 2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/20261012192940/https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349?hl=enGoogle:). Not in July–September captures.
- Docs editor Format › Text menu has no Letter spacing yet (checked Nov 7, 2026).
- Precedent: custom line spacing shipped to Docs and Slides together in Sept 2019 (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2019/09/line-spacing-docs-slides.html).
- No Workspace Updates announcement found yet. Strong signal, not a promise.


---

# About SVG to Slides

SVG to Slides turns SVG files into native, editable shapes inside Google Slides. Every path becomes its own shape: select it, recolour it with the standard fill picker, resize it without losing quality.

- Three ways in: Chrome extension (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi), web uploader (https://svgslid.es/convert), Google Slides add-on (https://svgslid.es/addon).
- The extension asks for no access to your Google account.
- Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

## Why it exists
Slides has no way to import an SVG; pasted SVGs flatten into images. Where there should be crisp icons and logos, there are crunchy PNGs.

## How it works
SVG to Slides writes Google Slides' own clipboard shape format from your SVG's paths. You paste, and Slides treats the result as native shapes. The extension converts inside your browser.

## Who builds it
Joe Gelman, independently. Contact: joe@glmn.co
